about: Places of interest stage 5: the famous places' own facts the map doesn't hold. Each finds its place by the word in its name (match) within km of at; kind, radius (m), tall (m), stones, banks, spire, banded, lintels, fallen, unlit say how it's drawn; note is what the sat nav says on arriving; add puts it in where the map hasn't got it. [stage 6] model names its own model, Data/RideUK/Sites/<model>.glb (Tools/make_ride_sites.py), drawn instead of the recipe, stood exactly at at and turned turn degrees clockwise. [churches stage 7] The well-known churches' notes: what the sat nav says on arriving, and their towers' and spires' heights (tall, spire), kept for the LiDAR stage.

sites.name: Castlerigg Stone Circle
sites.note: 38 stones, about 5,000 years old

sites.name: Swinside Stone Circle
sites.note: 55 stones, also called Sunkenkirk

sites.name: Long Meg and Her Daughters
sites.note: 59 stones, one of the largest circles in England

sites.name: Stonehenge
sites.note: Built about 2500 BC, lines up with the midsummer sunrise

sites.name: Avebury
sites.note: The largest stone circle in Britain, a village inside it

sites.name: Ring of Brodgar
sites.note: 27 of its 60 stones still standing

sites.name: Calanais Standing Stones
sites.note: 13 stones round a tall middle stone, about 5,000 years old

sites.name: Rollright Stones
sites.note: The King's Men, about 70 weathered stones

sites.note: Every stone lying down, inside a great bank

sites.name: Devil's Arrows

sites.name: Flamborough Head Lighthouse

sites.name: Beachy Head Lighthouse

sites.name: Souter Lighthouse

sites.name: St Bees Lighthouse
sites.note: On the cliffs at the start of the Coast to Coast walk

sites.name: Portland Bill Lighthouse

sites.name: Hoad Monument

sites.name: Captain Cook's Monument

sites.name: Hardy Monument

sites.name: Bolton Castle

sites.name: Maiden Castle

sites.name: British Camp

sites.name: Angel of the North

sites.name: Blackpool Tower

sites.name: Royal Liver Building

sites.name: York Minster

sites.name: Chesterfield, St Mary and All Saints
sites.note: The crooked spire, twisted and leaning nearly 3 m off true

sites.name: St Mary Redcliffe, Bristol
sites.note: Queen Elizabeth I called it the fairest parish church in England

sites.name: St Botolph's, Boston

sites.name: St James, Louth
sites.note: The tallest spire of any medieval parish church in England

sites.name: St Wulfram, Grantham

sites.name: Kilpeck, St Mary and St David

sites.name: Lavenham, St Peter and St Paul

sites.name: Long Melford, Holy Trinity

sites.name: Blythburgh, Holy Trinity

sites.name: Tewkesbury Abbey

sites.name: Bath Abbey

sites.name: Christchurch Priory
sites.note: The longest parish church in England

sites.name: Hexham Abbey
sites.note: Its crypt was built in 674 from Roman stones

sites.name: Selby Abbey

sites.name: Beverley Minster

sites.name: St Mary's, Whitby

sites.name: Haworth, St Michael and All Angels

sites.name: Stoke Poges, St Giles

sites.name: Iffley, St Mary

sites.name: Barfreston, St Nicholas

sites.name: Brixworth, All Saints

sites.name: Earls Barton, All Saints
sites.note: Its Saxon tower of about 970, striped with stone strips

sites.name: Greensted Church

sites.name: Escomb Church

sites.name: Bradford on Avon, St Laurence

sites.name: Patrington, St Patrick

sites.name: Heckington, St Andrew

sites.name: Ottery St Mary, St Mary

sites.name: Launceston, St Mary Magdalene

sites.name: Morwenstow, St Morwenna

sites.name: St Just in Roseland

sites.name: St Davids Cathedral

sites.name: St Govan's Chapel

sites.name: Rosslyn Chapel

sites.name: Iona Abbey

sites.name: Bolton Priory

sites.name: Kirkby Lonsdale, St Mary

sites.name: Eyam, St Lawrence
sites.note: The plague village: its rector shut it off from the world in 1665

sites.name: Tideswell, St John the Baptist

sites.name: Hathersage, St Michael
sites.note: Little John's grave is in its churchyard

sites.name: Ludlow, St Laurence
sites.note: The Cathedral of the Marches, its tower over the town

sites.name: Stratford upon Avon, Holy Trinity

sites.name: Painswick, St Mary
sites.note: 99 clipped yews in its churchyard, so the story goes

sites.name: Fairford, St Mary

sites.name: Cirencester, St John the Baptist

sites.name: Chipping Campden, St James
sites.note: A Cotswold wool church, its tower over the High Street

sites.name: St Martin's, Canterbury

sites.name: St Martin-in-the-Fields
sites.note: James Gibbs's church on Trafalgar Square, 1726

sites.name: St Bride's, Fleet Street

sites.name: St Bartholomew the Great

sites.name: Temple Church

sites.name: Wymondham Abbey

sites.name: Salisbury Cathedral

sites.name: Durham Cathedral

sites.name: Ely Cathedral

sites.name: Lincoln Cathedral

sites.name: Wells Cathedral
sites.note: Its scissor arches, and the west front's three hundred figures
